question: Does the fixed sequence-conditioned masked-feature candidate improve over the original frozen v1 topology encoder under the same converged probe budget?
timing: Supplement recorded while chromosome replication is running, before inspecting any of its held-out performance values. Execution health and artifact counts have been inspected. This does not alter that study or select candidate weights.
policy: Original v1 checkpoint per fold/seed, frozen encoder and NT. Refit identical native logistic probes using only original training/validation chromosomes; retain all 30 probe runs and save fitted artifacts. No historical output is overwritten. Every arm is compared to v1, without a performance-dependent gate.
validity: Replay every reference prediction and saved-model receipt; require convergence, original graph checks, identical target identities and bitwise C+S/C+S+H baseline predictions across old/new encoders. A mismatch is a blocker, not permission to silently filter examples.
inference: Reuse fixed replication scopes: primary A/C/D/E, development-exposed B separately, all five as sensitivity. Paired hierarchical fold/seed bootstrap, fold sign flips, BH within metric/scope. No architecture selection from these scores.
limitations: Model inputs and pretraining differ; comparison is between pipelines, not the isolated effect of masked reconstruction
The new representation E includes frozen sequence while original T is topology-native
Nominal epoch/compute budgets are not matched
Historical v1 biological results were previously inspected
The supplemental timing is disclosed; it was not part of the original four-arm development gate
